title: Clean corroded 12V battery terminals
machine: Car (any petrol, hybrid or EV with a 12V battery)
summary: White or green crust on the 12V battery terminals blocks current and causes slow cranking or no start. Clean them safely in the right order.
author: Ustad built-in

steps.title: Make it safe
steps.say: Engine off, key out, handbrake on. Put on gloves and eye protection.
steps.why: No current is flowing and the car cannot move while you work.
steps.safety: Battery acid burns skin and eyes. Never smoke or make sparks near a battery.

steps.title: Find the terminals
steps.say: Find the 12V battery. Positive is red or marked plus, negative is black or minus.
steps.why: The order you remove the clamps in is what keeps you safe, so you must know which is which.
steps.safety: In an EV or hybrid, touch only the small 12V battery. Never touch orange high-voltage cables.

steps.title: Negative off first
steps.say: Loosen and remove the NEGATIVE clamp first. Move the cable away from the battery.
steps.why: If your spanner touches the car body while the negative is off, there is no circuit, so no sparks.
steps.must_show: the black negative cable removed and lying clear of the battery terminal

steps.title: Then positive off
steps.why: With the negative already off, the positive can no longer short to the body.

steps.title: Scrub the crust
steps.say: Scrub terminals and clamps with baking soda, water and a wire brush.
steps.why: Baking soda neutralises the acid. The crust is an insulator that blocks starting current.
steps.safety: Keep the mix out of the battery vents.

steps.title: Rinse and dry
steps.say: Wipe with a little clean water, then dry everything completely.
steps.why: Leftover moisture and soda start new corrosion.

steps.title: Refit: positive, then negative
steps.say: Fit POSITIVE first, then NEGATIVE. Tighten until the clamps do not twist.
steps.why: The reverse order keeps the tool safe. A loose clamp causes the same no-start as corrosion.
steps.must_show: both clamps fitted tight: red cable on the positive post, black cable on the negative post, terminals clean

steps.title: Protect the terminals
steps.say: Put a thin layer of terminal grease or petroleum jelly on both terminals.
steps.why: It seals out air and moisture so corrosion comes back much slower.

steps.title: Test it
steps.say: Start the car. The battery warning light should go off.
steps.why: If it still cranks slowly, the battery itself may be weak. Test or replace it.

quiz.question: Why do you remove the NEGATIVE clamp first?
options: If your tool touches the car body, there is no short circuit
The positive is always more rusted
quiz.explain: The car body is connected to negative. With negative off, touching the body can't make a spark.

quiz.question: Why use baking soda?
quiz.explain: The crust is acidic; baking soda neutralises it so it can be washed away safely.

quiz.question: Corroded terminals usually cause…
quiz.explain: The crust resists the big current the starter motor needs.
